raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On HIP without AITER, `RMSNorm.forward_hip` uses vllm's RMSNorm kernels when vllm is installed and `forward_native` otherwise. AITER only supports CDNA, so on consumer RDNA GPUs (gfx11xx, gfx12xx) the native path is the one that runs. It is also the only one that works there today: the vllm branch has a call-signature bug that several open-then-closed PRs tried to fix (#31403, #21697, #41355, #31553), and none was merged.

`forward_native` writes RMSNorm as separate PyTorch ops, which launch **11 GPU kernels per call** (dtype casts, add, pow, mean, add-eps, rsqrt, two muls, cast back). At decode batch sizes each kernel processes a few KB, so the cost is launch and synchronization overhead, not math. With two norms per layer, that is roughly 700 kernels per token for a 32-layer model. #39725 noted the same cost ("a dozen pointwise kernels") on the batch-invariant path.

`torch.nn.functional.rms_norm` does the normalization in a single fused kernel; the residual add is one more. `forward_musa` already uses it.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`, `RMSNorm.forward_hip`, only in the `not _has_vllm_rms_norm` branch:

- `_can_use_torch_rms_norm` decides whether torch's `rms_norm` reproduces `forward_native`'s semantics. It falls back to `forward_native` for `post_residual_addition`, `var_hidden_size`, `cast_x_before_out_mul`, `fp32_residual`, `override_orig_dtype`, a weight dtype different from the input's, and batch-invariant mode.
- `_forward_torch_rms_norm` does the residual add and calls `nn.functional.rms_norm`. Like `forward_native`, it does not fuse `quant_linear`.

Nothing changes for CUDA, AITER (CDNA), vllm-backed HIP, or any other platform.

**Overlap with #46915:** that PR (against `amd_march`) fixes the vllm branch's call signature in the same `RMSNorm.forward_hip`; this one changes only the no-vllm branch. They're complementary and don't conflict on `main`; a backport of this PR to `amd_march` would need a small rebase onto it.

The eligibility check runs per call rather than being cached in `__init__`, because `cast_x_before_out_mul` is changed after construction in at least one model (`multimodal_gen/.../ming_image.py`). Decode replays captured CUDA graphs, so the check runs only during graph capture and prefill.

**Numerics:** the residual output is bit-identical to `forward_native`. The normalized output is not: the add is rounded to bf16 once before normalizing, while `forward_native` normalizes the unrounded fp32 sum. On gfx1151 (bf16, hidden size 3072), cosine similarity vs `forward_native` is 0.999996, max abs diff 0.016-0.031.

**Tests:** `test/registered/unit/layers/test_layernorm.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):

- `test_plain_case_avoids_forward_native_and_matches_it`: the plain case does not route to `forward_native` (a silent perf regression otherwise), matches it within bf16 tolerance, and returns a bit-identical residual.
- `test_modes_torch_rms_norm_cannot_express_keep_native_output`: for each of the 7 fallback conditions, `forward_hip` returns exactly `forward_native`'s output and dtypes.

To check the tests guard what they claim, each of 9 mutations was applied in turn and caught by the expected test: removing the fast path, dropping the residual add, and removing each of the 7 conditions.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware and software for my results (the gfx1201 results under Speed Tests are @vivienfanghuagood's): Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Strix Halo), torch 2.10.0+rocm7.13.0a20260513 (TheRock nightly), `--attention-backend triton --mem-fraction-static 0.5 --context-length 8192 --disable-overlap-schedule`. On `main`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1` was also needed: the lean decode-attention kernel requests 66560 B of shared memory and RDNA allows 65536, which is a separate issue.

**On `main` (bd5a445bf7), Phi-4-mini-instruct**, `sgl-eval` 0.1.3 GSM8K, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max tokens 1024, 32 threads. The baseline was run twice to measure run-to-run variation:

| Comparison | Accuracy | Questions that changed outcome | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline vs baseline rerun (same code) | 89.39% vs 88.93% | 36 | 0.41 |
| this PR vs baseline | 88.63% vs 89.39% | 34 | 0.12 |
| this PR vs baseline rerun | 88.63% vs 88.93% | 38 | 0.63 |

Even with greedy decoding, unpatched `main` changes 36 answers between two runs (batch composition differs at 32 concurrent requests). This PR's difference from the baseline is within that variation.

**On the #31137 branch** (with #31246 and the #31143 HIP-compat change applied), `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy. These were measured before `sgl-eval` became the recommended harness:

| Model | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Phi-4-mini-instruct | 83.0% | 83.0% |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat | 55.0% | 56.5% |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 76.5% | 75.5% |

gpt-oss-20b-bf16 was not scored: it is a reasoning model, and raw few-shot completion is not a valid check for it. A spot check with the chat template gave correct answers.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1`; 1-stream = 8 prompts at `--max-concurrency 1`, 8-way = 32 prompts at `--max-concurrency 8`. Same setup as the matrix in #31137.

**On `main` (bd5a445bf7), Phi-4-mini-instruct:**

| | Baseline | Baseline rerun | This PR | Change vs baseline mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-stream output tok/s | 18.04 | 18.18 | **19.97** | **+10.3%** |
| 1-stream mean TPOT (ms) | 54.53 | 54.17 | **49.22** | -5.1 ms |
| 8-way output tok/s | 116.54 | 117.05 | **122.99** | **+5.3%** |
| 8-way mean TPOT (ms) | 62.03 | 61.88 | **58.94** | -3.0 ms |

**On the #31137 branch** (setup as above):

| Model | Arch | 1-stream tok/s | 8-way tok/s | TPOT saved (1-stream) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phi-4-mini-instruct | dense | 18.43 -> 20.02 (+8.6%) | 118.8 -> 125.2 (+5.3%) | 4.6 ms |
| gpt-oss-20b-bf16 | MoE | 21.91 -> 24.11 (+10.0%) | 63.5 -> 65.0 (+2.2%) | 4.1 ms |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat | MoE + MLA | 13.65 -> 14.66 (+7.4%) | 44.1 -> 45.5 (+3.0%) | 4.9 ms |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | dense | 10.03 -> 10.56 (+5.3%) | 66.1 -> 69.2 (+4.8%) | 4.9 ms |

Llama-3.1-8B could not be served on `main` on this machine, with or without this PR. `main`'s HIP RoPE path keeps `cos_sin_cache` in fp32, and the locally built `sgl_kernel` (from the #31137 branch) expects bf16. That's unrelated to this change.

**gfx1201 (RDNA4), measured independently by @vivienfanghuagood** ([comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45540#issuecomment-6495357147)). Stock `rocm/pytorch` image (torch 2.10, no vllm, no AITER), so RMSNorm takes exactly the branch this PR changes. Base: `main` + #43679 (gfx1201 kernel build) + #47254 (RDNA default attention) + a local guard for the quark AITER imports; each arm is the base with or without this PR. Default server flags (Triton attention, decode CUDA graphs), two rounds alternating arms on the same GPU, `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids` 512 in / 256 out, GSM8K with `sgl-eval` 0.1.2, `enable_thinking=false`, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8:

| Qwen3-8B bf16 unless noted | Without this PR (round 1 / 2) | With this PR (round 1 / 2) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 output tok/s (median TPOT) | 25.03 / 25.02 (39.6 ms) | 28.91 / 28.92 (34.3 ms) | **+15.6%** |
| c=8 output tok/s (median TPOT) | 189.5 / 189.3 (40.6 ms) | 206.2 / 205.8 (37.5 ms) | **+8.8%** |
| GSM8K, 100 questions | 95% / 94% | 93% / 94% | within noise |
| OLMoE-1B-7B GSM8K, 50 questions | 64% / 54% | 66% / 66% | within noise |

The 5.3 ms TPOT drop matches the profile below: about 35 µs saved per call, times about 145 norms per token for Qwen3-8B (two per layer plus the Q/K norms, and the final norm).

**Profiling** (torch.profiler, one `RMSNorm` call with residual, bf16, hidden 3072, gfx1151):

| | GPU kernels | 64 calls in one CUDA graph |
|---|---|---|
| `forward_native` | 11 | 2.93 ms |
| this PR | 2 (`CUDAFunctor_add`, `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel`) | 0.67 ms |

The graph timing reuses the same inputs (hot L2). That matches serving here, since each norm's input was just written by the preceding kernel and is about 6 KB per token.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable: no user-facing behavior or flags change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). One deviation, explained under Modifications: the eligibility check is per call, not cached in `__init__`.

nodes.body: Hi maintainers, could someone add the run-ci label or trigger CI for this PR? The change only affects the HIP no-AITER/no-vllm path, plus a CPU unit test.

Gentle follow-up on CI for this one. All three latest runs (Base, Extra, AMD ROCm 10) show as failed, and I believe they’re from the gated/default runs rather than the change itself (happy to dig in if a maintainer sees otherwise). Could someone add run-ci or re-trigger?

Recap: on HIP without AITER or vLLM (consumer RDNA, e.g. gfx1151 / Strix Halo), RMSNorm.forward_hip falls back to forward_native, about 11 kernels per call. This PR uses torch.nn.functional.rms_norm instead (2 kernels), keeping forward_native for the cases torch’s op can’t match. Phi-4-mini on main: +10.3% single-stream, +5.3% 8-way; GSM8K within noise. CUDA, AITER, and vLLM-backed paths are unchanged.

It pairs with #46327 (gfx11 weight padding): this PR speeds up the non-GEMM part of decode, and that one speeds up the GEMMs. Thanks!

Validated on RDNA4 (gfx1201) in a stock `rocm/pytorch` image (torch 2.10, no vLLM, no aiter), so RMSNorm takes exactly the HIP fallback this PR changes.

- **Base:** current `main` + #43679 (gfx1201 kernel build) + #47254 (RDNA default attention) + a local guard for the quark aiter imports. Each arm is the base with or without this PR.
- **Model and flags:** Qwen/Qwen3-8B bf16 and OLMoE-1B-7B at default server flags (Triton attention, decode CUDA graphs).
- **Rounds:** two, alternating arms, same GPU.
- **Throughput:** `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 512/256.
- **Accuracy:** `sgl-eval==0.1.2` gsm8k, `enable_thinking=false`, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8.

| | without this PR (round 1 / 2) | with this PR (round 1 / 2) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B c=1 output tok/s (median TPOT) | 25.03 / 25.02 (39.6 ms) | 28.91 / 28.92 (34.3 ms) | **+15.6%** |
| Qwen3-8B c=8 output tok/s (median TPOT) | 189.5 / 189.3 (40.6 ms) | 206.2 / 205.8 (37.5 ms) | **+8.8%** |
| Qwen3-8B gsm8k (100 questions) | 95% / 94% | 93% / 94% | within noise |
| OLMoE-1B-7B gsm8k (50 questions) | 64% / 54% | 66% / 66% | within noise |

Rounds agree to within 0.2%. This is a clear decode win on RDNA, and accuracy is unchanged. Note: this PR and #46915 both edit `RMSNorm.forward_hip`. #46915 fixes the vLLM branch's call signature, while this PR changes the no-vLLM branch, so they're complementary, but whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

@vivienfanghuagood Thanks a lot, this is a great data point, and the first on RDNA4. The TPOT drop (39.6 → 34.3 ms) lines up with the per-call profile in the description: ~35 µs saved per norm × ~145 norms per token for Qwen3-8B (Q/K norms included) ≈ 5 ms. I’ll add your gfx1201 results to the description.

Good catch on #46915 . Agreed they’re complementary (that one fixes the vLLM branch, this one the no-vLLM branch). If this PR lands second, I’m happy to do the rebase.
@HaiShaw when you have a moment, could you pls take a look? It's the HIP no-vllm RMSNorm fallback, with gfx1151 and gfx1201 (by @vivienfanghuagood ) results in the description.

+    def _can_use_torch_rms_norm(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, post_residual_addition: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+    ) -> bool:
+        # Checked per call: some models flip cast_x_before_out_mul after construction.
+        return (
+            post_residual_addition is None
+            and self.variance_size_override is None
+            and not self.cast_x_before_out_mul
+            and not self.fp32_residual
+            and self.override_orig_dtype is None
+            and x.dtype == self.weight.dtype
+            and not is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+        )
+
+    def _forward_torch_rms_norm(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, residual: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+    ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+        # One rms_norm kernel (plus the add) instead of forward_native's ~11;
+        # like forward_native, quant_linear is not fused here.
+        if residual is not None:
+            residual = x + residual
+            x = residual
+        out = nn.functional.rms_norm(
+            x, (self.hidden_size,), self.weight, self.variance_epsilon
+        )
+        return out if residual is None else (out, residual)

+"""Unit tests for srt/layers/layernorm.py"""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers import layernorm
+from sglang.srt.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+HIDDEN = 64
+NUM_TOKENS = 4
+
+
+def _make_norm(weight_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16, **kwargs) -> RMSNorm:
+    norm = RMSNorm(HIDDEN, eps=1e-6, weight_dtype=weight_dtype, **kwargs)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        norm.weight.copy_(1.0 + 0.1 * torch.randn(HIDDEN))
+    return norm
+
+
+def _make_inputs() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    # The second half of each row is 10x larger, so a partial-row variance
+    # (var_hidden_size) differs clearly from the full-row one.
+    x = torch.randn(NUM_TOKENS, HIDDEN)
+    x[:, HIDDEN // 2 :] *= 10
+    return x.bfloat16(), torch.randn(NUM_TOKENS, HIDDEN).bfloat16()
+
+
+class TestRMSNormHipWithoutVllm(CustomTestCase):
+    """forward_hip with neither AITER nor vllm (e.g. RDNA): torch's rms_norm
+    where it matches forward_native's semantics, forward_native everywhere else."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        patcher = patch.object(layernorm, "_has_vllm_rms_norm", False)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def test_plain_case_avoids_forward_native_and_matches_it(self):
+        # Rerouting to forward_native is a silent decode regression on RDNA;
+        # the residual feeds the next layer, so it must match native exactly.
+        norm = _make_norm()
+        x, residual = _make_inputs()
+        expected = norm.forward_native(x)
+        expected_out, expected_residual = norm.forward_native(x, residual)
+
+        with patch.object(
+            norm, "forward_native", side_effect=AssertionError("native path taken")
+        ):
+            out = norm.forward_hip(x)
+            out_with_residual, new_residual = norm.forward_hip(x, residual)
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_with_residual, expected_out)
+        self.assertEqual(new_residual.dtype, expected_residual.dtype)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(new_residual, expected_residual))
+
+    def test_modes_torch_rms_norm_cannot_express_keep_native_output(self):
+        # Each mode changes the math or dtypes in ways torch's rms_norm does not
+        # reproduce, so forward_hip must return forward_native's exact result.
+        cases = {
+            "var_hidden_size": dict(norm_kwargs=dict(var_hidden_size=HIDDEN // 2)),
+            "cast_x_before_out_mul": dict(norm_kwargs=dict(cast_x_before_out_mul=True)),
+            "fp32_residual": dict(norm_kwargs=dict(fp32_residual=True)),
+            "override_orig_dtype": dict(
+                norm_kwargs=dict(override_orig_dtype=torch.float32)
+            ),
+            "weight_dtype_mismatch": dict(norm_kwargs=dict(weight_dtype=torch.float32)),
+            "post_residual_addition": dict(post_residual_addition=True),
+            "batch_invariant_mode": dict(batch_invariant=True),
+        }
+        for name, case in cases.items():
+            with self.subTest(mode=name):
+                norm = _make_norm(**case.get("norm_kwargs", {}))
+                x, residual = _make_inputs()
+                post = (
+                    torch.randn_like(residual)
+                    if case.get("post_residual_addition")
+                    else None
+                )
+                with patch.object(
+                    layernorm,
+                    "is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled",
+                    return_value=case.get("batch_invariant", False),
+                ):
+                    out, new_residual = norm.forward_hip(x, residual, post)
+                expected_out, expected_residual = norm.forward_native(x, residual, post)
+                self.assertEqual(out.dtype, expected_out.dtype)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, expected_out))
+                self.assertEqual(new_residual.dtype, expected_residual.dtype)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(new_residual, expected_residual))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body: Hi maintainers, could someone add the run-ci label or trigger CI for this PR? The change only affects the HIP no-AITER/no-vllm path, plus a CPU unit test.

Gentle follow-up on CI for this one. All three latest runs (Base, Extra, AMD ROCm 10) show as failed, and I believe they’re from the gated/default runs rather than the change itself (happy to dig in if a maintainer sees otherwise). Could someone add run-ci or re-trigger?

Recap: on HIP without AITER or vLLM (consumer RDNA, e.g. gfx1151 / Strix Halo), RMSNorm.forward_hip falls back to forward_native, about 11 kernels per call. This PR uses torch.nn.functional.rms_norm instead (2 kernels), keeping forward_native for the cases torch’s op can’t match. Phi-4-mini on main: +10.3% single-stream, +5.3% 8-way; GSM8K within noise. CUDA, AITER, and vLLM-backed paths are unchanged.

It pairs with #46327 (gfx11 weight padding): this PR speeds up the non-GEMM part of decode, and that one speeds up the GEMMs. Thanks!

Validated on RDNA4 (gfx1201) in a stock `rocm/pytorch` image (torch 2.10, no vLLM, no aiter), so RMSNorm takes exactly the HIP fallback this PR changes.

- **Base:** current `main` + #43679 (gfx1201 kernel build) + #47254 (RDNA default attention) + a local guard for the quark aiter imports. Each arm is the base with or without this PR.
- **Model and flags:** Qwen/Qwen3-8B bf16 and OLMoE-1B-7B at default server flags (Triton attention, decode CUDA graphs).
- **Rounds:** two, alternating arms, same GPU.
- **Throughput:** `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 512/256.
- **Accuracy:** `sgl-eval==0.1.2` gsm8k, `enable_thinking=false`, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8.

| | without this PR (round 1 / 2) | with this PR (round 1 / 2) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B c=1 output tok/s (median TPOT) | 25.03 / 25.02 (39.6 ms) | 28.91 / 28.92 (34.3 ms) | **+15.6%** |
| Qwen3-8B c=8 output tok/s (median TPOT) | 189.5 / 189.3 (40.6 ms) | 206.2 / 205.8 (37.5 ms) | **+8.8%** |
| Qwen3-8B gsm8k (100 questions) | 95% / 94% | 93% / 94% | within noise |
| OLMoE-1B-7B gsm8k (50 questions) | 64% / 54% | 66% / 66% | within noise |

Rounds agree to within 0.2%. This is a clear decode win on RDNA, and accuracy is unchanged. Note: this PR and #46915 both edit `RMSNorm.forward_hip`. #46915 fixes the vLLM branch's call signature, while this PR changes the no-vLLM branch, so they're complementary, but whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

@vivienfanghuagood Thanks a lot, this is a great data point, and the first on RDNA4. The TPOT drop (39.6 → 34.3 ms) lines up with the per-call profile in the description: ~35 µs saved per norm × ~145 norms per token for Qwen3-8B (Q/K norms included) ≈ 5 ms. I’ll add your gfx1201 results to the description.

Good catch on #46915 . Agreed they’re complementary (that one fixes the vLLM branch, this one the no-vLLM branch). If this PR lands second, I’m happy to do the rebase.
@HaiShaw when you have a moment, could you pls take a look? It's the HIP no-vllm RMSNorm fallback, with gfx1151 and gfx1201 (by @vivienfanghuagood ) results in the description.
